subject: Re: Redwood Private (VPC) pricing — post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@paymentsai.com>; Miranda Lopez <miranda.lopez@paymentsai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-25T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Private (VPC) pricing — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks for the sync earlier — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

Call recap:
- PaymentsAI needs a Private/VPC deployment for production workloads (data residency + SOC2)
- Primary use: customer support automation + payment reconciliation (batched inference + streaming)
- Expected steady-state token volumes: you mentioned roughs of tens of millions/month
- Important constraints: 3 environments (prod/stage/dev), SOC2 evidence, and annual contracting

Information we need to finalize pricing:
1) Target monthly token volume (best estimate or range) — this drives unit economics and discounts.
2) Budget range you have for the platform (ARR or monthly) so we can align licensing + consumption.
3) Preferred licensing model: subscription (annual platform fee + per-1M token unit) vs committed token blocks vs flat reserved capacity.
4) Support tier: Standard vs Premium (SLA, 24/7, designated CSM) — affects fee.

Our proposed next steps:
- Evan/Miranda: send us estimated token volumes (best/worst case) and a target $/1M tokens if you have one.
- We (Ben) will prepare a pricing options sheet (attached draft) showing: baseline platform fee, per-1M token unit economics, committed discount tiers, and environment add-on pricing.
- If the numbers look good, we can draft a mutual action plan and get legal looped for a 12-month subscription + support.

Attachments: redwood-proposal-paymentsai-v1.xlsx (pricing ranges, licensing options)

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@paymentsai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Miranda Lopez <miranda.lopez@paymentsai.com>
Date: 2027-02-25T17:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Private (VPC) pricing — post-call recap & next steps

Ben — thanks for the summary and the docs. A couple of specifics from our side to help you model pricing:

Estimated volumes (month):
- Low: 20M tokens/month (pilot + early customers)
- Mid: 50M tokens/month (Q3 target)
- High: 150M tokens/month (post-product-market-fit projection)

Budget context:
- We're looking to keep operating costs predictable. Internal target: ~ $1,000 per 1M tokens (i.e., $1k/1M) as a unit economics goal — but we're flexible if committed pricing and reasonable platform fees reduce that.

Licensing preference:
- Prefer annual subscription with committed discounts (helps procurement).
- Need pricing impact for adding more environments (we will want 3 initially; potential additional sandbox environments later).

Support & compliance:
- Required: SOC2 Type II evidence.
- Support: Standard is OK for now; may upgrade to Premium if usage/SLAs require.

Next ask: can you include a line-item that shows per-1M token cost at each commit tier (20M, 50M, 150M) and a separate row for environment add-ons? Also confirm whether quantized model variants / batching would change the unit token cost materially.

Thanks — Evan
Evan Brooks
Head of Platform
PaymentsAI

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@paymentsai.com>
Cc: Miranda Lopez <miranda.lopez@paymentsai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-26T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Private (VPC) pricing — post-call recap & next steps

Evan — got it, this is very helpful. Attached is a slightly updated pricing sheet that maps the three commit tiers you listed to unit economics and shows environment-add pricing and support tiers. High level:

Option A — Annual subscription + committed tokens (recommended)
- Platform fee (annual): $40,000 (includes control plane, initial onboarding, SOC2 evidence package)
- Token unit price (per 1M) at tiers:
  - 20M commit: $1,200 / 1M
  - 50M commit: $900 / 1M
  - 150M commit: $650 / 1M
- Environment add-on: $6,000 per additional non-prod environment (prod included). Your 3 envs = base + 2 x $6k = $52k platform fee shown pro-rated in year 1.
- Support: Standard included; Premium (24/7 + dedicated CSM) = +$30k/yr

Option B — Reserved capacity (predictable throughput)
- Reserved cluster pricing based on GPU count; example quote for your mid-case (50M tokens) included. Better for very high sustained throughput and predictable latency.

Notes on cost drivers and optimizations:
- Quantized model variants and KV/prefix caching reduce GPU compute per-token. In practice, quantization + batching could lower effective $/1M by ~10-30% depending on model and prompt shape. We show an illustrative 20% tech-optimization discount in the updated sheet.
- Unit economics in the sheet assume average prompt length and a 3x caching efficiency for repeat prefixes (conservative).

Next steps:
1) I'll update the sheet with a line showing your exact commit numbers (20/50/150) and a committed-discount path.
2) If that looks good, Marissa will put together a mutual action plan and draft term summary for legal.
3) We can get a preliminary SOW and SOC2 evidence timeline once we agree on model and support tier.

Attached: redwood-proposal-paymentsai-v1.xlsx (v2 with tiers), mutual-action-plan-paymentsai.pdf

Ben

From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@paymentsai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Miranda Lopez <miranda.lopez@paymentsai.com>
Date: 2027-02-26T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Private (VPC) pricing — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Ben — this looks reasonable. Quick clarifications before we show finance:
- Does the platform fee scale linearly with environment count? We want an example for 5 envs.
- Can you quantify the 20% tech-optimization discount example: i.e., for the 50M tier, what would final $/1M look like after quantization + batching?

Also, procurement will want a rough timeline for SOC2 artifacts (when can we get evidence/access to the report) and an initial draft of terms to validate legal redlines.

Evan

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@paymentsai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-27T09:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Private (VPC) pricing — post-call recap & next steps

Evan — answers inline:
- Environment scaling: platform fee is per-deployment bundle. Non-prod envs are charged at a lower add-on rate (we used $6k/env as an example). For 5 envs the math in the sheet would be: base $40k + (4 x $6k) = $64k annual platform fee. We can provide a stepped discount if you plan >5 envs.
- 50M tier after tech optimizations: $900 / 1M (base) -> approx $720 / 1M after a 20% optimization (quantization + batching). With a committed discount pathway and annual prepay we could get closer to ~$600 / 1M at scale (this is illustrative; we'll model exacts once we have usage telemetry).
- SOC2 timeline: we can provide the current SOC2 Type II report within 2 weeks of NDA and provide onboarding evidence and the controls matrix as part of the onboarding package (Marissa will coordinate).
- Terms & SOW: Marissa will produce a mutual action plan and a term summary in the next 48 business hours; legal draft follows.

I'll update the pricing sheet to show the 5-env example and the post-optimization line for each commit tier. If you're comfortable, I'll mark this as next-stage MQL -> sales-accepted and assign Marissa to follow up with MAP + terms.

Ben
